evals.prompt: Review PR 615. A new service sets a non-column attribute on loaded ticket models for the API resource to read. On main, another service already does the same to categories (hydrate sets group_position), and the ticket repository sets listed_by_promoter the same way. The standards ban accessors, mutators and $appends only.
evals.expected_output: No Structure finding about the attribute: the PR follows existing precedent and no standard forbids it.
expectations: Searches main for the same pattern before considering a Structure finding
Does not report the non-column attribute as a finding
Does not stretch the accessor and mutator rule to cover it

evals.prompt: Review PR 610. The ticket says existing bundles shouldn't change. The diff lets sell-together bundles skip the free-ticket display cap; on main a cap of 1 shows one ticket of a bundle that must be bought whole, main already exempts those bundles from listing rotation, and the PR body says whole-bundle listings stay visible when caps would hide them.
evals.expected_output: No flag for the cap change: the PR body, main's precedent and the feature itself answer why.
expectations: Answers why the author made the change from the PR body, main's handling and the feature's needs before considering a flag
Does not raise the cap change as a Decision or ask whether it is intentional
Does not treat the ticket's 'existing bundles shouldn't change' line alone as a reason to flag
Leaves the cap change out of the report and the draft comments

evals.prompt: Review PR 611. The ticket says nothing changes for existing bundles, and the linked product doc says buyers must buy every ticket of a sell-together bundle. The PR body says a locked ticket shouldn't count towards a bundle, so with one of four tickets locked, checkout now sells the other three on their own; main refused them. Nothing in the feature needs locked tickets left out.
evals.expected_output: One Decision: quote the ticket and doc next to the PR body's reason and ask which should win.
expectations: Does not drop the candidate just because the PR body states the reason
Treats the author's reason as a policy choice rather than something the feature needs
Raises it as a Decision quoting the ticket or product doc and the PR body side by side
Asks the author directly which behaviour it should have, not whether it is intentional
Does not ask whether the change was agreed with, approved by, or checked with a ticket owner or anyone else

evals.prompt: Review PR 613. The coding standards ban business logic and queries in JSON resources. The PR adds a bundle-quantity call to EventResource::toArray, which on main already runs a query and reads the cache in the same method.
evals.expected_output: No Structure flag: the same method on main already breaks the standard the same way.
expectations: Checks how the same file handles it on the merge base
Drops the candidate because main's EventResource::toArray already breaks that standard the same way
Leaves it out of the report and the draft comments

evals.prompt: Review PR 612. Checkout and the event page each build their own query for the tickets a bundle counts. The two queries return the same tickets for every case today; one could drift if someone later adds a scope to only one of them. This diff does not add either query.
evals.expected_output: No Structure flag: the cost is hypothetical and the copies agree today.
expectations: Checks whether the two queries disagree on any real case
Drops the candidate as hypothetical because they agree today and the diff adds neither copy
Leaves it out of the report and the draft comments

evals.prompt: Review PR 482. Its repository has a saved worktree command, and one candidate is a checkout rule that now accepts a partial bundle.
evals.expected_output: The candidate is reproduced against base and head in a temporary review worktree before it is reported as Critical.
expectations: Creates the review worktrees with the saved command to reproduce the candidate
Checks the worktree's head matches the PR's head commit
Runs an untracked scratch test or script that prints the values on the path and compares base with head
Confirms the fixture reached the path before trusting the result
Deletes the scratch files and removes the base worktree before reporting
Keeps the head worktree and appends its removal command to the session's cleanup file
Names the base and head results on the Critical line
Stops every site and background process it started and checks none is left

evals.prompt: Review PR 483. The PR's branch is already checked out in a worktree the user made earlier, and one candidate needs a run on base and head.
evals.expected_output: The user's worktree is untouched; the head run happens in a new worktree on a temporary review-head branch.
expectations: Does not add files, seed data, or run anything in the user's existing worktree
Creates the head review worktree on a temporary branch review-head-<n> at the PR's head commit
Never registers the user's worktree for removal

evals.prompt: Review PR 77 in a repository with no saved worktree command. One candidate looks critical.
evals.expected_output: The review runs from fetched refs with no checkout, and the candidate is marked as traced, not reproduced.
expectations: Creates no worktree and switches no branch
Reads the change through fetched refs
Says the Critical finding is traced, not reproduced

evals.prompt: Review PR 482. It adds a query inside a JSON resource that runs once per ticket, and two classes with near-identical names in the same namespace. No standards file mentions either.
evals.expected_output: Both are flagged with their concrete cost.
expectations: Flags the per-ticket query with the query it runs per row
Flags the near-identical names, naming what a reader confuses
Does not drop either for lacking a named standards rule

evals.prompt: Review PR 482. Its ticket says no existing behaviour changes, and the PR body says it now hides locked tickets from every listing count on purpose.
evals.expected_output: The change is flagged with the acceptance criterion it contradicts, not as a defect.
expectations: Flags the change as Needs an answer, not as a defect
Names the acceptance criterion it contradicts
Backs the before and after with saved runs on the merge base and the PR head

evals.prompt: Review PR 482. The user's voice and brand files are saved. Validation leaves one critical defect and two structural problems.
evals.expected_output: The fixed HTML report: the PR's gist, a plain-language journey of the change with each flag pinned to its step, and a drill-down per flag down to the exact diff lines, opened for the user.
expectations: Builds the report with the skill's build script from its template, the brand CSS, and the clone, into the reports directory
Gives each flag repository paths and head-commit lines, so its code links open the real code and the PR diff
Starts with a TL;DR of two or three sentences on what the PR does, with no review content
Writes the steps from the users' side, naming each actor (buyer, seller, admin, promoter or other), with no class names or ticket numbers outside the code drill-down
Gives each flag code locations whose highlighted lines are the problem itself, each with a plain note
Checks the page at desktop and phone widths and fixes anything unreadable before opening it
Opens the report and replies in chat with its path, the TL;DR, and one-line flags
Lists the critical defect first in the review result, then the two code-quality problems
Builds the final page only after a claims audit passes on that exact data, and shows the audited badge
Writes each flag in the voice file's style, with the problem and its direct reason in one or two sentences
Omits dropped candidates, counts, and the standards read

evals.prompt: Review PR 482 and leave the comments on it for the author.
evals.expected_output: The findings and the draft review go to the user in the report and chat only.
expectations: Posts nothing to GitHub
Drafts the review and line comments in the report, phrased as questions to the author
Reports only validated findings with file and line on the head commit

evals.prompt: The report for PR 482 is open. The user says: post that review.
evals.expected_output: The exact review is shown, and posted as one review once the user confirms that text.
expectations: Shows the review state, body, and line comments that will be posted, and waits for the go
Posts one review with inline comments only on lines in the diff
Appends the saved signature to the body
Reports the review's URL and posts nothing else

evals.prompt: Which PRs are waiting on my review? Nothing has been configured yet.
evals.expected_output: The organisation is asked for, saved, and the list shown.
expectations: Asks which organisation to search
Saves the answer so the next run does not ask
Lists the open PRs requesting the user's review and asks which to take
